answer: Sequential work receipts. Each identity must submit a unique, verifiable trace of real computation—a nonce found over a rolling onyx difficulty target—before its next action is accepted. Traces chain through a shared canyon of prior outputs, so forged identities can't reuse another's history. A valid trace costs hours of dedicated compute plus a rare opal-tier hardware attestation bound to one device. An attacker scaling to N identities pays N times that compute and needs N distinct attested devices, making mass fabrication physically expensive rather than merely costly in tokens.
